I will do my best to complete my cross-examination within the extra session we have, but I cannot guarantee that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: That was all I wanted confirmation of, Mr. Krgovic. We haven't gotten to the question of protective measures yet. But the -- I just needed to know whether counsel for the Defence was on board with the -- what I understand to be the -- what we are going to do, that we will be begin on the assumption that, with the extra session, we could complete this witness. And once we -- I appreciate that you don't know exactly where you're going to go. I fully understand that. But the common agreement is that there's a possibility that we could so complete and, therefore, we will begin. Now, the matter of the application, which is before us.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. A motion was filed yesterday and I don't think there's been a formal response from the Defence in the short time-frame. The witness is ready to address Your Honours directly on his concerns, if you so require. It's one of the situations we've become familiar with over the past few months where the witness raises the issues arriving here in The Hague for the first time and his concerns are set out in the motion and if Your Honour would say like more clarification or particulars, he is ready to address you formally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So although the Defence would not have had an opportunity to respond because of the recency of the filing, we propose to adopt the usual course of calling the witness in and examining him and the Defence will have an opportunity, if they wish, to ask any questions before we rule. Yes, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before the witness is brought into the courtroom, if the witness will testify to the adjudicated facts in respect of which he has been called, and if he will testify to the matters as envisaged, the Defence will have no problems with that. Adjudicated facts do not require protective measures. However, if the witness will testify to what has been stated under paragraph 3 of this motion about Stojan Zupljanin and other matters, we will have difficulty with that, because the Prosecutor's intention is to go beyond the scope of matters the witness was called for to begin with, and this is the third or the fourth witness who has had his scope of testimony expanded. And it is through the back door in the third half-time, so to speak, that the OTP seems to attempt to have evidence admitted. And that's the problem I have with this course of procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we will go into closed session to hear the witness's -- to hear the witness on the application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Inasmuch as the ruling that was made just before the adjournment was made in closed session, I now repeat it in open session and it also provides the opportunity to clarify what may not have been clearly articulated at the time it was delivered. The only application on which the Chamber rules is the application for protective measures in respect of the witness who is about to be called, and -- but the Chamber anticipates that what was highlighted in the written motion that it will, in the course of this witness's testimony, also have to rule on the question of whether the Prosecution will be permitted to ask questions beyond the specified adjudicated facts dealing with a particular meeting, which is -- the details of which appear in the motion. And the anticipated ruling that the Chamber may give on that, which was a factor in the ruling that it makes, in terms of protective measures, is that the witness is afforded the protective measures of a pseudonym, and voice and face distortion. And in respect that separate ruling, it is by a majority; Judge Harhoff dissenting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The -- I believe we already have the witness's name and ethnicity on the record. If we could go into private session so that the usual preliminary questions can be asked by the Bench and then we will revert to open session, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pidwell, do you intend to go into the takeover as such?

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Is that within the scope of adjudicated facts? I suppose you're referring to 521, but there the takeover is only mentioned as a date. That's -- that's a time-line.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: 520 is the adjudicated fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Pardon?

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Yes, sir. And it talks about the involvement of the police in the takeover on the 11th of June. This witness will give evidence about his detention on that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It talks about -- about the involvement -- the involvement of the -- of the police in detaining Serbs and Croats; right? Not the takeover as such.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, that -- that's correct. I'm going to ask him questions about the day before, what he was doing, and what happened to him personally on that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So the question is whether, in your submission, this falls within the -- having regard to our earlier rulings which I needn't repeat at this stage, whether this is within the context of the adjudicated facts indicated. We -- the -- I -- I come back to where we began, that we haven't yet ruled on whether you would be permitted to do that and you needn't repeat what you would have said. It's just that we need to make a ruling for the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I have, in fact, covered that, Your Honour, already. I intend now to go to the essence of the adjudicated fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The -- questions I thought you had covered that. I wasn't sure where we were going. Because it would have been necessary for me to indicate for the record that the permission for you to go -- to lead that was a majority decision in which Judge Harhoff -- Judge Delvoie dissented. So although it is after the fact, I'm, nevertheless, putting it in for the record. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Sir, we are in open session now, so if you could just please be careful in -- not to mention any names or any facts that can potentially identify you; and if we get into some difficulty, we will go back into closed session. Without saying what position you held, did you go to work on the 10th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Was there anything unusual that occurred on that day that draw -- was drawn to your attention, or was it just a normal working day?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a normal working day.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Was your boss present at work on that day?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And was your deputy present at work on that day?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Do you recall what time you went home?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went home after work, around 4.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And did anything unusual occur that night that was brought to your attention?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing unusual until 11.00 in the evening, when all the lights went out in town and all the telephone lines got cut off.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Had that happened previously in your area, or was this the first time?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The electricity would get cut off if the weather was bad, but that wasn't very often. This would have happened if circumstances were bad. And the same thing happened this night.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: The next day, what time did you leave your home to go to work?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: (redacted). And from further away, I could hear shooting. It was a Muslim holiday, Bajram. There's a village above Kotor Varos called Ravne and I thought that after the morning prayer people were celebrating their religious holiday by shooting in the air. That was a custom in Bosnia-Herzegovina. As I walked further towards the police station, near the primary school I noticed some armed men, and they had red berets on their heads. They had flakjackets, leather gloves, long-barrelled, and with insignia of Republika Srpska. They also had short-barrelled weapons and handcuffs. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... could we redact, please, page 71, lines 9 to 11 and also lines 21 to 23. I think at this juncture it may be better to go back into private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back kin open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: We are in open session now and when you answer my questions please be careful not to identify yourself by mentioning the position you occupied or any names, et cetera. Use formations like, The place which I -- where I worked, and, My job, et cetera. Now, at the last set of questions from Ms. Pidwell was based on that video film of your interrogation. Basically, in that video footage, you did not say anything that would incriminate you. You did not imply yourself in any of the illegal activities, such as arming, and you did not say you had any direct knowledge about the distribution of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that in no way, by no action, or word, did I incriminate myself or participate in any way in preparations for armed insurgency. I always tried to be a professional and act professionally, although I was not a career policeman. I thought that a policeman should treat everyone equally, Serb, Croats, and Muslims. And I never participated in any form of self-organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And in this video we see when you say, I have no direct knowledge, that's the first thing you say, I have no direct knowledge, nor did I in any way participate in the distribution of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What I said in that interview is, as we termed it in the police, for public purposes. And I said what I heard from the rumours, from street talk, what was going around, what stories circulated in pubs and bars and in the streets. I also heard from one HDZ session that the HDZ had those radio stations. Shall I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I'll show you the transcript of what you are quoting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see -- it's 65 ter 672. Tab 16 in the Zupljanin Defence binder. Not to be broadcast, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, did you say tab 16?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, 15, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: 15. Yes, I see it now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Sir, this is from a meeting. I will not say of which body. You can see that. And here among the people present, you see your name. Look at the top. 5th of March; right?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see my name. I was invited to that meeting. It's an expanded meeting of the HDZ held on 5 March 1992. I was invited to present the security situation in the area of Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Look at the agenda. Paragraph AD 1, second paragraph, and the last sentence says: "We also have communications, so it will be easier to inform all check-points." That's true; right?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a reference to those radios. Now we live in modern times, we all have cell phones, but at that time the municipality of Kotor Varos was very badly covered by the public telephone network. I don't know what the party meant with this. If they had already been preparing for war, it was much too early and very sensitive. And from what I know, there were communications between HDZ party leaders in various villages, because, at that time, the -- the municipality was not fully covered by telephone. And these communications, of course, could be also used for war purposes. And when we were detained in Maslovare, we asked Mr. Pejic to have secret negotiations with Mr. Mato Bjelobrk, who was supposed to organise the surrender of these radio -- radio stations. I don't know whether that talk ever took place, because I was detained but I know this man, Bjelobrk, was later killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. It's about these radio stations but even I did not know these details until I came to that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Sorry, Your Honours, I don't think the question was recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I noticed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, sir, my question was not recorded because all -- because of all there turning off and turning on of microphones. I asked you if these were the radio stations discussed at this meeting. Are they the same radio stations that you mentioned in the video - that was the essence of my question - right?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can I have an exhibit number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As exhibit number 2 -- okay. As Exhibit 2D00-129, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Apart from that interview -- in fact, do you remember whether everything was recorded in that video or were you questioned beyond what was shown in the footage.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the video shows it all.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And in that interview, as far as I was able to see, you did not say anything that could incriminate you or could indicate your participation in anything illegal.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in no way involved, so I could not incriminate myself, and I always assumed that if I got involved in something, it couldn't be good for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: The Prosecution asked you about your status, if you were a policeman or a military man. And I'll ask you about a certain quandry we have about certain documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have 2D13 shown to the witness, please. This is a list from the Croatia Republic of Herceg-Bosna, the defence ministry, a list of persons recorded in the Defence Department or the draft office of Kotor Varos. Can we show ERN -- I won't tell you which number of the page it is for a reason. It's ERN 0714620. 0071-4620. [In English] Can we go to a private session for a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, for the record, we are back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sir, we thank you for your assistance to the Tribunal. You are now released as a witness and we wish you a safe journey back to your home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good-bye.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And the shutters can be raised again. We are grateful to the interpreters, the court reporters, the remainder of the support staff, and, indeed, the accused themselves for accommodating the witness who, otherwise would have had to have been -- would have had to remain here over what would have been an extended weekend in order to complete his testimony. So we will take the adjournment now, to reconvene in this courtroom on Monday afternoon, at what point we are scheduled to receive the testimony by videolink of a witness. We are in receipt of a motion from the Prosecution in terms of protective measures in respect of that witness and we would begin on Monday afternoon by asking the Defence for their oral responses to that -- to that application, which they would have had the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Unless, of course, they're in a position to do it now. But I didn't ... So we aren't pressing you to do it now, but as I said we get your responses on Monday afternoon. There is one small matter that does concern the Chamber, Ms. Pidwell, and it is the experience with the witness who has just been released, in that the modified protective measures and having to go into private session for such an extended period of his testimony, when, effectively, the entire testimony is taken in closed session so that is something we would have to bear in mind in the future, should we have to consider future applications. But we take the adjournment now to Monday afternoon, and I wish everyone a safe weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 22nd day of November, 2010, at 2.15 p.m. 25
